questions.question: If the price of the item is increased by 70% and then allows a scheme discount of 5% and 20% on this marked price. If price is paid in cash and an additional discount of 20% is allowed, then what is his gain percentage?

questions.question: The cost price and the marked price of an item are Rs. 720 and Rs. 900 respectively. When it is sold at a discount of x%, the profit is \(\frac{5x}{3}\%\) . What is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: The cost price and the marked price of an item are Rs. 720 and Rs. 900 respectively. When it is sold at a discount of x%, the profit is \(\frac{5x}{3}\%\). What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Given:

CP = Rs. 720

MP = Rs. 900

Concept used:

SP = MP × (100 - discount)/100

SP = CP × (100 + profit)/100

Calculation:

According to the question,

900 × (100 - x)/100 = 720 × (100 + 5x/3)/100

⇒ 900 × (100 - x) = 720 × (100 + 5x/3)

⇒ 90000 - 900x = 72000 + 1200x

⇒ 90000 - 900x = 72000 + 1200x

⇒ 2100x = 18000

⇒ x = 18000/2100

⇒ x = 60/7

⇒ x = \(8\frac{4}{7}\)

∴ The vale of x is \(8\frac{4}{7}\)

questions.question: A seller marks an item for Rs. 500 and sells it at a discount of 25%. He also gives a gift worth Rs. 65. If he still makes 24% profit, then the cost price of the item (in Rs.) is:
questions.questionHtml: A seller marks an item for Rs. 500 and sells it at a discount of 25%. He also gives a gift worth Rs. 65. If he still makes 24% profit, then the cost price of the item (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked price = Rs. 500

Discount = 25%

Gift worth = Rs. 65

Profit = 24%

Formula used:

1. Selling price after discount = Marked price × (1 - Discount%)

2. Cost price = (Selling price - Gift) / (1 + Profit%)

Calculation:

Step 1: Calculate the selling price after a 25% discount.

⇒ Selling price = 500 × (1 - 0.25)

⇒ Selling price = 500 × 0.75 = Rs. 375

Step 2: Subtract the value of the gift from the selling price to get the effective selling price.

⇒ Effective selling price = 375 - 65 = Rs. 310

Step 3: Calculate the cost price using the profit formula.

⇒ Cost price = 310 / (1 + 0.24)

⇒ Cost price = 310 / 1.24 = Rs. 250

∴ The cost price of the item is Rs. 250.

questions.question: Two successive discounts of 40% and 20%, respectively, on the marked price of an article are equal to single discount of Rs 988. The marked price (in Rs) of the article is:
questions.questionHtml: Two successive discounts of 40% and 20%, respectively, on the marked price of an article are equal to single discount of Rs 988. The marked price (in Rs) of the article is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Two discounts = 40% and 20%

Formula:

Two discounts a% and b%

Total discount = \((a +b)- \frac{ab}{100}\)

Discount amount = (marked price) × (discount %)/100

Calculation:

Single discount percentage = \((40 +20)- \frac{40× 20}{100}\) = 52%

⇒ 52 = 988/marked price × 100

⇒ Marked price = 1900

∴ Marked price of an article is Rs.1900.

Alternate MethodLet the MP be x.

x - [x × (100 - 40)/100 × (100 - 20)/100] = 988

⇒ x - [x × (60/100) × (80/100)] = 988

⇒ x - x × (3/5) × (4/5) = 988

⇒ 13x/25 = 988

⇒ x = (988 × 25)/13

⇒ x = 1900

∴ Marked price of an article is Rs.1900.

questions.question: Reema sold 48 articles for Rs. 2,160 and suffered a loss of 10%. How many articles should she sell for Rs. 2,016 to earn a profit of 12%?
questions.questionHtml: Reema sold 48 articles for Rs. 2,160 and suffered a loss of 10%. How many articles should she sell for Rs. 2,016 to earn a profit of 12%?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the formula: (Price1 ÷ (Articles1 × (100 − Loss%))) = (Price2 ÷ (Articles2 × (100 + Profit%)))

2,160 ÷ (48 × 90) = 2,016 ÷ (n × 112)

2,160 ÷ 4,320 = 2,016 ÷ (n × 112)

1 ÷ 2 = 2,016 ÷ (n × 112)

n × 112 = 4,032 ⇒ n = 4,032 ÷ 112 = 36

∴ The correct answer is 36 articles.

Alternate Method

Given: Selling Price (SP1) = Rs. 2,160 for 48 articles, Loss = 10%. Target Profit = 12% for SP2 = Rs. 2,016.

Formulas: CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%) | SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

⇒ SP of 1 article = 2,160 ÷ 48 = Rs. 45

⇒ CP of 1 article = 45 × (100 ÷ 90) = Rs. 50

⇒ Required SP of 1 article for 12% profit = 50 × (112 ÷ 100) = Rs. 56

⇒ Number of articles for Rs. 2,016 = 2,016 ÷ 56 = 36

∴ The correct answer is 36 articles.

Additional Information

Unitary Method in P&L

When solving for multiple articles, it is often easiest to find the Cost Price (CP) of a single unit first.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise in the question.

questions.question: Three merchants, A, B and C, sell sewing machines at the same list price. Merchant A allows two successive discounts of 30% and 16%; merchant B allows two successive discounts of 20% and 26%, and merchant C allows two successive discounts of 25% and 20%. Which merchant should a customer choose to get the maximum discount?
questions.questionHtml: Three merchants, A, B and C, sell sewing machines at the same list price. Merchant A allows two successive discounts of 30% and 16%; merchant B allows two successive discounts of 20% and 26%, and merchant C allows two successive discounts of 25% and 20%. Which merchant should a customer choose to get the maximum discount?

options.text: Either merchant B or merchant C
options.html: Either merchant B or merchant C

questions.solution:
Given:

Merchant A allows two successive discounts of 30% and 16%

Merchant B allows two successive discounts of 20% and 26%

Merchant C allows two successive discounts of 25% and 20%

Concept used:

Successive discount:

If a person gives two successive discounts on the markup price x% and y% respectively.

Then Selling price = Markup price × [(100 - x)/100] × [(100 - y)/100]

Calculation:

Let the list price of three merchants A, B and C be Rs. x

The selling price of the merchant A = x × [(100 - 30)/100] × [(100 - 16)/100] 

⇒ x × [70/100] × [84/100]

⇒ x × 0.7 × 0.84

⇒ x × 0.588

⇒ Rs. 0.588x

The selling price of the merchant B = x × [(100 - 20)/100] × [(100 - 26)/100] 

⇒ x × [80/100] × [74/100]

⇒ x × 0.8 × 0.74

⇒ x × 0.592

⇒ Rs. 0.592x

The selling price of the merchant C = x × [(100 - 25)/100] × [(100 - 20)/100] 

⇒ x × [75/100] × [80/100]

⇒ x × 0.75 × 0.80

⇒ x × 0.6

⇒ Rs. 0.6x

From the above, we can see the merchant A selling price is less than both B and C.

So, for a customer, buying an article from merchant A gives the maximum discount.

∴ A customer will choose merchant A to get the maximum discount 

Alternate Method

Calculation:

Let the list price of three merchants A, B and C be 100 unit

The selling price of the merchant A = 100 × [(100 - 30)/100] × [(100 - 16)/100] 

⇒ 100 × [70/100] × [84/100]

⇒ 100 × 0.7 × 0.84

⇒ 100 × 0.588

⇒ 58.8 unit

The selling price of the merchant B = 100 × [(100 - 20)/100] × [(100 - 26)/100] 

⇒ 100 × [80/100] × [74/100]

⇒ 100 × 0.8 × 0.74

⇒ 100 × 0.592

⇒ 59.2 unit

The selling price of the merchant C = 100 × [(100 - 25)/100] × [(100 - 20)/100] 

⇒ 100 × [75/100] × [80/100]

⇒ 100 × 0.75 × 0.80

⇒ 100 × 0.6

⇒ 60 unit

From the above, we can see the merchant A selling price is less than both B and C.

So, for a customer, buying an article from merchant A gives the maximum discount.

∴ A customer will choose merchant A to get the maximum discount 

Concept used: 

Effective discount percentage:

If If a person gives two successive discounts on the markup price x% and y% respectively.

Then the effective discount percentage = x + y - (xy/100)

Calculation:

The effective discount percentage for Merchant A = 30 + 16 - (30 × 16)/100

⇒ 46 - (480/100)

⇒ 46 - 4.8

⇒ 41.2%

The effective discount percentage for Merchant B = 20 + 26 - (20 × 26)/100

⇒ 46 - (520/100)

⇒ 46 - 5.2

⇒ 40.8%

The effective discount percentage for Merchant C = 25 + 20 - (25 × 20)/100

⇒ 45 - (500/100)

⇒ 45 - 5

⇒ 40%

From the above, we can see the merchant A effective discount percentage is more than merchant B and merchant C.

So, for a customer, buying an article from merchant A gives the maximum discount.

∴ A customer will choose merchant A to get the maximum discount

questions.question: On selling an article for Rs. 115, the gain is 20% more than the loss incurred on selling it for Rs. 104. If the article is sold for Rs. 130.80, then the profit percentage is:
questions.questionHtml: On selling an article for Rs. 115, the gain is 20% more than the loss incurred on selling it for Rs. 104. If the article is sold for Rs. 130.80, then the profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
Let CP of the article be Rs. X.

According to the question

(115 – x) = (x – 104) × 120/100

5(115 – x) = 6(x – 104)

575 – 5x = 6x – 624

6x + 5x = 624 + 575

11x = 1199

x = 1199/11

x = 109

CP of the article = Rs. 109

New SP of the article = Rs. 130.80

Profit percentage = (130.80 – 109)/109 × 100 = 20%

Alternate Method Gain/Loss = (100 + 20)/100

⇒ 120/100 = 6/5

In both cases Cost price will be same.

⇒ S.P1 - Gain = S.P2 + Loss

⇒ 115 - 6x = 104 + 5x

⇒ 6x + 5x = 115 - 104

⇒ 11x = 11

⇒ x = 1

Putting x = 1 

⇒ 115 - 6 = 109 that is C.P.

New SP of the article = Rs. 130.80

Profit percentage = (130.80 – 109)/109 × 100 = 20%

questions.question: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 25% when he sells an article by allowing 20% discount on its marked price. If the cost price of the article is decreased by 20%, how much discount percent should he allow now on the same marked price so as to earn the same percentage of profit as earlier?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 25% when he sells an article by allowing 20% discount on its marked price. If the cost price of the article is decreased by 20%, how much discount percent should he allow now on the same marked price so as to earn the same percentage of profit as earlier?
questions.solution:
Given :

A shopkeeper gained 25% while allowing 20% discount 

Formula used :

Selling price = Marked price - discount on marked price 

Selling price = cost price + profit on cost price 

Calculations :

Let the initial cost price be 100x 

Selling price = 100x + 25% of 100x 

⇒ 125x 

Selling price = Marked price - 20% of marked price 

Marked price = 625x/4 = 156.25x

Now Cost price got decreased by 20%, so new cost price 

New cost price = 80x 

New selling price = 80x + 25% of 80x 

⇒ 100x 

Discount per cent on marked price to get this selling price 

Discount per cent = (Marked price - selling price)/(Marked price) × 100 

⇒ (156.25x - 100x)/(156.25x) × 100 

⇒ 36% 

∴ Discount should be 36% 

Shortcut Trick MP / CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 - Discount%)

According to the question,

⇒ MP / CP = (100 + 25) / (100 - 20) = 125 / 80

CP = 80 , now CP is decreased by 20%

So, the new CP = 80 × (100 - 20)/100 = 64 

Now, using the new CP = 64 and MP = 125  

⇒ 125 / 64 = (100 + 25) / (100 - Discount%)

⇒ 125 / 64 = 125 / (100 - Discount%)

⇒ 100 - Discount% = 64 

⇒ Discount% = 100 - 64 = 36%

∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: Ramesh sells an article for Rs. 34,440, after allowing an 18% discount on the marked price and still manages to gain 40% profit. If Ramesh sold the article at a 12% discount on the marked price, then what will be his profit, correct to two places of decimals?
questions.questionHtml: Ramesh sells an article for Rs. 34,440, after allowing an 18% discount on the marked price and still manages to gain 40% profit. If Ramesh sold the article at a 12% discount on the marked price, then what will be his profit, correct to two places of decimals?
questions.solution:
CP = 34,440 / (1 + 0.40) = CP = 34,440 / 1.40 = CP = ₹24,600

MP = 34,440 / (1 - 0.18) = MP = 34,440 / 0.82 = MP = ₹42,000

New SP = MP × (1 - 0.12) = 42,000 × 0.88

New SP = ₹36,960 = New Profit = (New SP - CP) / CP

New Profit = (36,960 - 24,600) / 24,600 × 100

New Profit = 0.5024 × 100 = 50.24%

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 30% higher than the cost price and allows a discount of 10% on the marked price. In order to earn 6.5% more profit, what discount percent should he allow on the marked price?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marks his goods 30% higher than the cost price and allows a discount of 10% on the marked price. In order to earn 6.5% more profit, what discount percent should he allow on the marked price?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial Profit% = 30 − 10 − (30 × 10 ÷ 100) = 17%.

New required Profit% = 17 + 6.5 = 23.5%.

Let new discount be d%. Using effective change formula: 30 − d − (30d ÷ 100) = 23.5.

6.5 = 1.3d ⇒ d = 6.5 ÷ 1.3 = 5%.

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Alternate Method

Given: Markup = 30%, Initial Discount = 10%, Additional Profit required = 6.5%.

Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 | MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100

⇒ Let CP = 100. Then Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 30% of 100 = 130.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP) = 130 − 10% of 130 = 130 − 13 = 117.

⇒ Initial Profit = 117 − 100 = 17.

⇒ New Profit required = 17 + 6.5 = 23.5. New SP = 100 + 23.5 = 123.5.

⇒ New Discount Amount = MP − New SP = 130 − 123.5 = 6.5.

⇒ New Discount Percent = (6.5 ÷ 130) × 100 = 5%.

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Additional Information

Markup and Discount Relation

The relationship between Cost Price and Marked Price can be expressed as: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Effective Profit Percentage

When a markup of m% and a discount of d% are applied, the Net Profit% = m − d − (md ÷ 100).

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers a discount of 24 % on the marked price. On a special sale day, he offers an extra 30% off coupon after the first discount. If the article was sold for Rs. 7 ,700.70. What is the marked price in Rs. of the article?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper offers a discount of 24 % on the marked price. On a special sale day, he offers an extra 30% off coupon after the first discount. If the article was sold for Rs. 7 ,700.70. What is the marked price in Rs. of the article?
questions.solution:
Given:

Discount 1 = 24%

Discount 2 = 30%

Selling Price (SP) = ₹7,700.70

Formula Used:

Let Marked Price (MP) = ₹x

Price after first discount = x × (1 - 24/100)

Price after second discount = [x × (1 - 24/100)] × (1 - 30/100)

Given, Price after both discounts = SP

Calculation:

SP = [x × (1 - 24/100)] × (1 - 30/100)

⇒ 7,700.70 = x × 0.76 × 0.70

⇒ 7,700.70 = x × 0.532

⇒ x = 7,700.70 / 0.532

⇒ x = 14,475

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: What is a single discount (to the nearest whole number) equivalent to the successive discounts of 10%, 17% and 25% ?
questions.questionHtml: What is a single discount (to the nearest whole number) equivalent to the successive discounts of 10%, 17% and 25% ?
questions.solution:
Given:

Discounts = 10%, 17% and 25%

Calculation:

Single discount = 100 - [(100 - 10)/100 × (100 - 17)/100 × (100 - 25)/100] × 100

= 100 - 90/100 × 83/100 × 75/100 × 100

= 43.97 ≈ 44%

∴ Single discount of 44%.

questions.question: Two successive discounts each of x % on the marked price of an article are equal to a single discount of Rs. 350. If the marked price of the article is Rs. 800, then the value of x is:
questions.questionHtml: Two successive discounts each of x % on the marked price of an article are equal to a single discount of Rs. 350. If the marked price of the article is Rs. 800, then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Two successive discounts each of x % on the marked price of an article are equal to a single discount of Rs. 350.

Marked price of the article is Rs. 800.

Concept used:

If two successive discount of A% is given, then the resultant or effective single discount is (A + A - A2/100)%

Middle term factor

Calculation:

According to the question,

800 × (2x - x2/100)% = 350

⇒ (2x - x2/100) = 175/4

⇒ x = 25

∴ The value of x is 25.

questions.solution:
⇒ 20 = \(S.P. - 560\over 560\) × 100 ⇒ S.P. = Rs 672

questions.question: Two successive increments of 30% each is by what percentage more than two successive decrements of 30% each? (Correct to two decimal places)
questions.questionHtml: Two successive increments of 30% each is by what percentage more than two successive decrements of 30% each? (Correct to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
Single equivalent increase of 30% each = 30 + 30 + [(30 × 30)/100] = 30 + 30 + 9 = 69%

Single equivalent decrease of 30% each = 30 + 30 - [(30 × 30)/100] = 51%

Required percentage = [(69 - 51)/51] × 100  = 18/51 × 100 = 35.29%

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 5320. It is subject to two successive discounts, the first being 15%, and the second at a rate of 20% of the first. What is the selling price (to nearest Rs.) of the article?
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of an article is Rs. 5320. It is subject to two successive discounts, the first being 15%, and the second at a rate of 20% of the first. What is the selling price (to nearest Rs.) of the article?
questions.solution:
Given:

The marked price = Rs. 5320

Two successive discounts = 15%, and the second at a rate of 20% of the first.

Formula used:

Single discount on two successive discounts = (a + b – ab/100)

Calculation:

Let the selling price be 100

According to the question

The second at a rate of 20% of the first = (20% of 15)

⇒ (20/100 × 15) = 3%

Now, single discount on two successive discount = (a + b – ab/100)

⇒ (15 + 3 – 15 × 3/100)

⇒ (18 – 0.45) = 17.55%

Now, (100 – 17.55)% = 82.45%

Selling price = (82.45% of 5320)

⇒ (82.45/100 × 5320)

⇒ (438634/100)

⇒ Rs. 4386.34 ~ Rs. 4386

∴ The required selling price is Rs. 4386

Mistake PointsNote the language of the question

"second at a rate of 20% of the first " which means 20% of 15 = 3%.

Don't take the second discount = 20 %. 

Alternate MethodGiven that, the marked price is Rs. 5320

According to the question

The second at a rate of 20% of the first = (20% of 15)

⇒ (20/100 × 15) = 3%

Hence, the selling price 

SP =  \(5320× (1-\frac{15}{100})(1-\frac{3}{100})\)

⇒ SP = (5320 × 85 × 97)/10000

⇒ SP = 4386

questions.question: A shop keeper sold an article at four-fifth of the marked price and suffered a loss of \(3 \frac{1}{3}\) %. Find the profit percent, if he sold the article at the marked price. (correct to nearest integer)
questions.questionHtml: A shop keeper sold an article at four-fifth of the marked price and suffered a loss of \(3 \frac{1}{3}\)%. Find the profit percent, if he sold the article at the marked price. (correct to nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Given:

The shopkeeper sold the article at four-fifth of the marked price

Loss incurred is 10/3%

Concept used:

Selling price = Cost price × (1 - loss percentage/100)

Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Percentage profit = (Profit/Cost price) × 100%

Calculation:

Let the marked price & cost price of the article be 145P & C respectively.

The selling price of the article = 145P × 4/5 = 116P

According to the question,

C × (1 - 10/300) = 116P

⇒ C × 29/30 = 116P

⇒ C = 120P

If sold at the marked price, then earned profit = (145P - 120P) = 25P

Then,

the percentage profit = (25P/120P) × 100% = 20.833% ≈ 21%

∴ The profit percent, if he sold the article at the marked price is 21%.

 

Alternate Method 

MP : SP = 5 : 4 

Let the MP be 500, then SP = 400

Loss% = 10/3% (Fractional value = 1/30)

CP = 30 units

SP = 30 - 1 = 29 units (given as 400)

29 units = 400

30 units = (400/29) × 30 = Rs. 413

If the article sold at MP

MP = New SP = 500

Profit = 500 - 413 = 87

∴ Required Profit% = (87/413)/100 = 21%

questions.question: A sells an article to B at a loss of 20%, B sells it to C at a profit of 12.5% and C sells it to D at a loss of 8%. If D buys it for Rs. 248.40, then what is the difference between the loss incurred by A and C’?

questions.question: An article is marked Rs.224 above its cost price. It was sold at a profit of 20% after giving a discount of 15% on its marked price. What is the selling price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.questionHtml: An article is marked Rs.224 above its cost price. It was sold at a profit of 20% after giving a discount of 15% on its marked price. What is the selling price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.solution:
Formula used:

SP = MP × (1 - D%)  

where 

MP = Marked Price

SP = Selling Price

D% = Discount

CP = \(SP\over 100+G\) × 100

where 

CP = Cost Price

SP = Selling Price

G = Gain %

Calculation:

Let the marked price be "a".

SP = a × (1 - 0.15) = 0.85a

Similarly, CP = \(0.85a\over 120\) × 100 = 0.7083a

Difference between MP and CP = a - 0.7083a = 0.2917a

According to the question, difference between CP and MP is Rs 224

⇒ 0.2917a = Rs 224

⇒ a = \(224\over 0.2917 \) = Rs 768

∴ SP = 0.85a = 0.85 × 768 = Rs 652.80

∴ The selling price of the article is Rs 652.80.

questions.question: One–third of goods are sold at a 15% profit, 25% of the goods are sold at a 20% profit and the rest at a 20% loss. If the total profit of Rs. 138.50 is earned on the whole transaction, then the value (in Rs.) of the goods is:
questions.questionHtml: One–third of goods are sold at a 15% profit, 25% of the goods are sold at a 20% profit and the rest at a 20% loss. If the total profit of Rs. 138.50 is earned on the whole transaction, then the value (in Rs.) of the goods is:
questions.solution:
Given:

One–third of goods are sold at a 15% profit

25% of the goods are sold at a 20% profit

The rest at a 20% loss

Concept used:

Profit from each part = quantity × profit percentage

Calculation:

Let the total number of articles be 120.

Let the cost price of 120 articles be 120 unit

1/3rd of 120 = 40 and 1/4th of 120 = 30 and Rest = 120 – 40 – 30 = 50

Total profit = 40 × (15/100) + 30 × (20/100) – 50 × (20/100) = 6 + 6 – 10 = 2 unit

2 unit = 138.50

⇒ 1 unit = 69.25

⇒ 120 unit = 69.25 × 120 = Rs. 8310
